work_items.title: Foundation: pure route-leg / offer-view / camera modules, mapCamera promote-to-shared shim, and all new driver i18n keys across 6 locales
files_touched: web/src/shared/map/mapCamera.ts (new — moved verbatim from features/customer/shell/mapCamera.ts, incl. LatLng, LatLngBounds, CameraIntent, cameraIntent, MIN_CAMERA_ZOOM)
web/src/shared/map/mapCamera.test.ts (new — moved verbatim; imports updated to './mapCamera')
acceptance_criteria: PROMOTE mapCamera via the sanctioned shim pattern (mirrors features/customer/order/priceQuote.ts -> shared/pricing/interpretQuote): move the FULL contents of features/customer/shell/mapCamera.ts (LatLng, LatLngBounds, SetViewIntent, FitBoundsIntent, CameraIntent, CameraInput, MIN_CAMERA_ZOOM, cameraIntent) to a NEW web/src/shared/map/mapCamera.ts; move mapCamera.test.ts alongside it (fix its import to './mapCamera'); then REDUCE features/customer/shell/mapCamera.ts to exactly `export * from '../../../shared/map/mapCamera'` (a re-export shim). This means ZERO customer import statements change — all ~11 existing consumers (CustomerMapBackground, CustomerMapShell, TrackingPage, MapOrderPage, orderCamera, suggestLocation, useSuggest, DestinationSearch, markerInterpolation, etc.) resolve through the shim. tsc is the verification nothing dangled. The driver code imports LatLng/cameraIntent from '../../../shared/map/mapCamera' (NEVER cross-feature from customer). Do NOT re-point the customer imports; the shim exists precisely so they don't churn.

NEW pure module features/driver/ride/routeLeg.ts: `export type RouteLeg = 'toPickup' | 'toDropoff' | null` and `export function selectRouteLeg(input: { status: string, hasDropoff: boolean }): RouteLeg`. Rules (mirror rideButtonState's status vocabulary — Accepted/Arrived/InProgress): Accepted -> 'toPickup'; Arrived -> 'toPickup' (the leg drawn is still the pickup approach until Start); InProgress -> hasDropoff ? 'toDropoff' : null (skip when no dropoff, matching rideButtonState's navAction=hasDropoff?'navigate':null); every other status (Free/Offline/New/Assigned/Completed/Cancelled/unknown) -> null. Also export a pure `export function legEndpoint(leg: RouteLeg, order: { pickupLat, pickupLng, dropoffLat: number|null, dropoffLng: number|null }): { lat: number, lng: number } | null` returning pickup coords for 'toPickup', dropoff coords for 'toDropoff' (null if dropoff missing), null for null. No leaflet import, no react import — pure.

NEW pure module features/driver/offer/offerCardState.ts: `export type OfferCardPhase = 'offer' | 'declining' | 'expired'` and a pure `export function offerActionOutcome(kind: 'success'|'stale'|'offline'|'noReason', current: OfferCardPhase): { nextPhase: OfferCardPhase, dismissAfterMs: number | null, showOffline: boolean, showStale: boolean, showReasonError: boolean }` capturing the OfferTakeover accept/decline result -> UI-transition decision (success -> dismiss immediately/dismissAfterMs=0; stale -> showStale + dismissAfterMs=2000; offline -> showOffline, stay; noReason -> showReasonError, stay). This lifts the branchy logic out of the component so WI-2 stays presentational and unit-testable. Do NOT import react/leaflet.

NEW pure module features/driver/map/driverMapView.ts: `export function selectDriverMapCamera(input: { own: LatLng|null, legStart: LatLng|null, legEnd: LatLng|null }): LatLng[]` returning the non-null points to frame ([own, legEnd] during a ride so both driver and target are visible; [own] when only own known; [] when nothing) — feeds cameraIntent (from shared/map/mapCamera) at the call site. Pure; imports only the LatLng TYPE from '../../../shared/map/mapCamera'. This is the driver analog of TrackingPage's cameraTarget = [carMarker, pickupMarker].filter(...) line.

ADD every new i18n key WI-2/WI-3/WI-4/WI-5 will consume to ALL SIX locale JSONs (cs-CZ authoritative; en-US/ru-RU/uk-UA/fil-PH/de-DE translated) so locales.parity.test.ts stays green and the parallel component WIs never touch locale files. work_items.title: Top offer box: redesign OfferTakeover full-screen dialog into a map-overlay top card (no on-accept navigation)
acceptance_criteria: NEW component OfferCard.tsx (props: { dto: OrderDetailDto, expiresAt: string, onDismiss: () => void }) rendered as a TOP overlay CARD (not position:fixed inset:0 full-screen; a card anchored top with safe-area top padding, styled via theme tokens only). It is NOT role='dialog'/aria-modal (that was the takeover); use role='region' with aria-label={t('driver.offer.boxLabel')} plus role='alert' on the stale/offline banners. It composes exactly the existing pieces: CountdownRing (expiresAt + totalSeconds computed once on mount = max(1, round((new Date(expiresAt)-Date.now())/1000)), onExpired -> onDismiss after a 2s expired message — preserve today's behavior), PriceBadge, useOfferRoute(dto.pickupLat,dto.pickupLng) for distance+ETA (render via driver.offer.distanceEta), DeclineReasons in the declining phase.

Accept: reuse useOfferAccept -> accept(dto.id). On outcome.type==='success' call onDismiss() ONLY — DO NOT navigate. (Behavior change vs OfferTakeover which did navigate('/driver/ride'); there is no /driver/ride after this UC — the shared /driver screen reactively renders the ride view from useActiveOrderStore + useDriverMe once accept updates the store.) On 'stale' -> show stale banner + onDismiss after 2000ms. On 'offline' -> show offline hint, stay open. Route the phase/decision through offerCardState.offerActionOutcome (WI-1) rather than inline branches.

Decline: reuse useOfferDecline + DeclineReasons with the reason-required step; 'success'->onDismiss, 'stale'->banner+dismiss, 'noReason'->reason error, 'offline'->offline hint. Preserve the existing double-tap guards (the useOfferAccept/useOfferDecline hooks own isPending; disable the buttons while pending) and the two-phase offer->declining->back UX.

Preserve sound/vibration: call useOfferSound(phase === 'offer') exactly as OfferTakeover does; do not change the driver:newOrderOffered plumbing or useOfferListener (untouched — hosted in DriverLayout).

a11y: axe clean; the Accept button is the prominent primary >= theme.touchTargets.primary (64px), Decline >= theme.touchTargets.min (48px); every string via t() (informal 'ty' keys already in place from WI-1); icon-only/decorative elements aria-hidden. No color-contrast reliance (use approved token pairs).

This WI does NOT touch DriverLayout, router, or locale JSON. It exports OfferCard for WI-5 to mount; WI-5 swaps DriverLayout's <OfferTakeover/> for <OfferCard/> and removes OfferTakeover.tsx. Verify via vitest (mock useOfferAccept/useOfferDecline/useOfferRoute/useOfferSound and the api client per web-testing.md#network-mocking).
test_cases: OfferCard.test.tsx: renders pickup address, dropoff, PriceBadge, and a countdown; getByRole('region', { name: 'Nova objednavka' }) present; NOT role='dialog'.
Accept success -> accept(dto.id) called, onDismiss called, and useNavigate is NOT called (assert the navigate spy has 0 calls — pins the no-navigation behavior change).
Accept stale -> stale banner (role='alert') visible, onDismiss called after advancing fake timers 2000ms.
Accept offline -> offline hint visible, onDismiss NOT called, card stays.
Decline without reason -> reason error shown, decline NOT called; then pick a reason -> decline(dto.id, reason) called; success -> onDismiss.
Double-tap: with isPending true the Accept button is disabled (no second accept call).
Expiry: advance fake timers past totalSeconds -> expired message then onDismiss after 2000ms.
axe: expect(await axe(container)).toHaveNoViolations() via the configured helper.
work_items.notes: The ONE substantive behavior change is removing navigate('/driver/ride') on accept — encoded as a dedicated no-navigation test. Everything else is a re-skin of OfferTakeover's proven logic into a top card + extraction of the branch logic into offerCardState (WI-1). Optional 'draw driver->pickup line while offer shown' (spec section 2) is deferred to WI-5 composition (the map component is WI-3); OfferCard itself renders no map. Parallel-safe with WI-3/WI-4 (disjoint files).

work_items.title: DriverMapInner: lazy react-leaflet map with route Polyline (from geo/route geometry) + own/pickup/dropoff markers + camera controller
files_touched: web/src/features/driver/map/DriverMapInner.tsx (new — the ONLY driver-side leaflet importer; default export for React.lazy)
web/src/features/driver/map/DriverMapInner.test.tsx (new — mocks react-leaflet, never mounts a real MapContainer)
web/src/features/driver/map/useRouteGeometry.ts (new — eager hook, NO leaflet, fetches geo/route geometry for the active leg)
acceptance_criteria: NEW DriverMapInner.tsx: a PRESENTATIONAL default-export component (props only — coords + geometry, never a fetch). Props: { own: LatLng|null, pickup: LatLng|null, dropoff: LatLng|null, routeGeometry: number[][] | null, cameraTarget: LatLng[] | null, ariaLabel?: string }. It renders <MapyMap ariaLabel={ariaLabel ?? t('driver.map.label')}> with, as CHILDREN: a react-leaflet <Polyline positions={routeGeometry as [number,number][]}> when routeGeometry has >=2 points (the FIRST Polyline in the codebase — CustomerMapBackground only draws markers); <Marker> for own (blue dot icon, reuse RideMapInner's OWN_ICON svg), pickup (green PICKUP_ICON), dropoff (red DROPOFF_ICON); and a headless CameraController (copy the CustomerMapBackground CameraController pattern — useMap() + cameraIntent from shared/map/mapCamera + a prev-key ref) applying cameraTarget. Module-level divIcon consts (no useMemo). This is the ONLY module under features/driver/ that imports MapyMap/react-leaflet/leaflet — loaded via React.lazy from WI-5, so leaflet never enters the eager /driver chunk (rules/web-performance.md#code-splitting). Do NOT statically import it anywhere eager.

NEW useRouteGeometry.ts: an EAGER hook (NO leaflet import) that, given { leg: RouteLeg, own: LatLng|null, order }, computes the leg endpoint (legEndpoint from WI-1) and fetches getGeoRoute({fromLat:own.lat, fromLng:own.lng, toLat:end.lat, toLng:end.lng}) returning { geometry: number[][] | null, durationSeconds: number | null, isLoading }. Refetch when the leg changes (status change) — significant-movement refetch is OPTIONAL and NOT required (spec section 3 'at minimum fetch on status change'). Degrade silently on getGeoRoute throw (502 Geo.RouteUnavailable) -> geometry null (map still shows markers). Skip the fetch entirely when leg is null or own/endpoint missing. Keeps the geo/route call + geometry contract in eager, unit-testable code; DriverMapInner only renders what it is handed.

DriverMapInner unit test MOCKS react-leaflet (MapContainer -> stub that renders children AND carries role='application' + forwards aria-label per the CLAUDE.md UC-014 WI-2 aria-prohibited-attr trap; TileLayer/Marker/Polyline -> stubs exposing their props via data-attrs; useMap -> a stub) and mocks './useGeoConfig'/'./leafletSetup' as MapyMap's test does — NEVER mount a real MapContainer in jsdom (CLAUDE.md UC-010 WI-15). Assert the Polyline stub receives the geometry positions when >=2 points and is absent when geometry is null/<2 points.

a11y: the map region has an i18n aria-label; the mocked MapContainer stub carries role='application' so axe's aria-prohibited-attr does not fire (CLAUDE.md CustomerMapBackground.test.tsx reference). axe clean on the mocked render.

This WI does NOT touch DriverLayout, router, or locale JSON (keys come from WI-1). Leaflet-in-dist verification is deferred to WI-5 npm-build (WI-3 cannot verify the chunk until WI-5 wires the lazy import); WI-3 verifies via vitest with react-leaflet mocked.
test_cases: DriverMapInner.test.tsx: routeGeometry with 3 points -> Polyline stub rendered with those positions; routeGeometry=null -> no Polyline; routeGeometry=[[a,b]] (1 point) -> no Polyline (needs >=2).
DriverMapInner.test.tsx: own+pickup+dropoff all present -> three Marker stubs; own only -> one Marker; dropoff null -> no dropoff Marker.
DriverMapInner.test.tsx: axe clean (MapContainer mock carries role='application').
useRouteGeometry.test.ts: leg='toPickup' with own+pickup -> getGeoRoute called with own->pickup coords; returns geometry+duration from the mocked client.
useRouteGeometry.test.ts: leg=null -> getGeoRoute NOT called, geometry null.
useRouteGeometry.test.ts: getGeoRoute throws (502) -> geometry null, isLoading false, no throw to the caller (degrade).
useRouteGeometry.test.ts: leg changes toPickup->toDropoff -> a refetch fires with the new endpoint.
work_items.notes: Presentational/leaf split mirrors the customer precedent (CustomerMapBackground presentational + eager hooks feed it). The Polyline is genuinely new coverage (customer background is markers-only). CameraController is copied, not shared, from CustomerMapBackground — it is a react-leaflet-coupled controller that MUST live inside the lazy chunk (the PURE cameraIntent it calls is the shared/map/mapCamera module from WI-1). Parallel-safe with WI-2/WI-4.

work_items.title: Ride BottomSheet: Arrive/Start/Complete/No-show controls + ETA + Navigate handoff, driven by rideButtonState + useRideTransition
acceptance_criteria: NEW RideSheet.tsx wraps shared/ui/BottomSheet (ariaLabelKey='driver.ride.sheetLabel', open when an active order exists, expanded toggled by parent/local state, onClose collapses). Props: { order: OrderDetailDto, noShowEnabled: boolean, noShowCountdownSeconds: number|null, etaMinutes: number|null, onArrive, onStart, onComplete, onNoShow, isPending, pendingCount: number, reconciledNote: boolean }. It renders: pickup/dropoff addresses + tap-to-call phone (from DriverRidePage), an ETA line (driver.ride.etaToPickup for Accepted/Arrived, driver.ride.etaToDropoff for InProgress; omit when etaMinutes null), the PendingBadge (pendingCount), the reassigned banner (role='alert', t('driver.ride.reassigned')) when reconciledNote, and the action buttons.

Buttons via deriveRideButtons(order.status, noShowEnabled, noShowCountdownSeconds, hasDropoff) -> RideButton for Arrive/Start/Complete + No-show, exactly as DriverRidePage wires them (primary -> onArrive/onStart/onComplete by primaryAction; secondary noShow -> onNoShow). Complete's handler is onComplete (the parent WI-5 navigates to '/driver/ride/complete' — that route is KEPT; RideSheet does not navigate itself). A prominent Navigate button = <NavHandoff lat lng label labelKey={buttons.navLabel}> toward the current target (pickup while Accepted/Arrived, dropoff while InProgress if hasDropoff) — reuse buildNavUrl + the settings nav-app preference unchanged.

Offline/queue intact: the parent passes isPending from useRideTransition; RideSheet renders the PendingBadge (pendingCount prop, sourced from useQueuePendingCount in WI-5) as DriverRidePage does. RideSheet is PRESENTATIONAL for transitions — it does NOT call useRideTransition or useQueuePendingCount itself; WI-5 owns the hooks + the runTransition/'stale'->reconciledNote logic and passes handlers/flags down. This keeps the offline queue + reconcile + mid-ride reassignment machinery in one place (WI-5) and RideSheet unit-testable with plain handler spies.

a11y: BottomSheet already provides role='dialog' + i18n aria-label + focus-in-on-open + Escape -> onClose + focus restore (non-modal, keeps the Mapy logo reachable). Primary action >= theme.touchTargets.primary; nav/secondary >= theme.touchTargets.min; >=8px spacing; axe clean. Every string via t() (informal 'ty' keys from WI-1). Money ' Kc' cs-CZ, ETA via i18n {{min}} template.

This WI does NOT touch DriverLayout, router, useRideTransition, or locale JSON. It exports RideSheet for WI-5. Verify via vitest (mock the api client / no real network; use fake timers for any countdown display; prefer asserting the NavHandoff anchor href over mocking buildNavUrl).

work_items.title: Assembly: map-first /driver screen (shell + OfferCard + DriverMapInner + RideSheet), DriverLayout swap, router wiring, and removal of DriverHomePage/DriverRidePage/OfferTakeover/RideMapStrip
files_touched: web/src/app/DriverLayout.tsx (edit — swap OfferTakeover->OfferCard; keep useFleetHub/useOfferListener/DriverPositionReporter/DriverQueueBar/silent-refresh boot; make <Content> position:relative so the map absolute-fills it; render BottomNav only when there is no active ride so it does not collide with the ride BottomSheet)
web/src/app/router.tsx (edit — /driver renders DriverMapScreen; REMOVE the 'ride' child route + DriverHomePage/DriverRidePage imports; keep ride/complete, history, settings, login)
web/src/features/driver/ride/RideMapInner.tsx (REMOVE — superseded by DriverMapInner; grep-confirm no other importer first)
acceptance_criteria: NEW DriverMapScreen.tsx is the single map-first /driver screen. LAYOUT CONTRADICTION RESOLVED (advisor): the map must NOT be `position:fixed; inset:0` like CustomerMapShell — the customer map screens are SIBLINGS of CustomerLayout (no nav chrome to fight), but DriverMapScreen NESTS under DriverLayout whose BottomNav is a normal-flow flex child. A fixed-inset map would paint OVER the BottomNav (History/Settings unreachable — breaks AC#5). Instead the map fills the DriverLayout <Content> flex region: the screen is `position:relative; width:100%; height:100%` (Content is flex:1) with a MapLayer `position:absolute; inset:0; z-index:map` and overlay slots `position:absolute; z-index:overlay` with safe-area padding — full-bleed WITHIN the content region, BottomNav stays in flow below it. The map is DriverMapInner loaded via React.lazy (const DriverMapInner = lazy(() => import('./DriverMapInner'))) inside a <Suspense fallback={null}> — the ONLY place DriverMapInner is imported, so leaflet stays out of the eager /driver chunk. It reads own position via useOwnPositionStore(s => s.position) with an ATOMIC one-field selector (CLAUDE.md laneB3c zustand-object-selector loop trap — never a {a,b} object selector).

State-driven overlay by useDriverMe status + active-order state (mirror deriveHomeState vocabulary): Offline -> bottom panel with VehicleSelector + 'Zacit smenu' (useGoOnline) + geolocation-permission prompt as DriverHomePage does today; Free -> minimal 'Cekam na objednavku' indicator (role='status', REUSE driver.home.status.waitingForOrder) + 'Ukoncit smenu' (useGoOffline); Busy/EnRoute (active ride) -> the RideSheet ride view. CRITICAL (advisor): the Offline/Free panels are IN-SCREEN OVERLAY SLOTS (absolute-positioned within the map/Content region, bottoming out at the Content edge ABOVE the in-flow BottomNav which is VISIBLE in these states because order==null) — they must NOT be shared/ui/BottomSheet (position:fixed bottom:0) instances; only the ride view (WI-4 RideSheet) uses BottomSheet, and only then does BottomNav hide. Do NOT copy the RideSheet BottomSheet pattern for the Offline/Free panels or they overlap the visible nav. MAP HEIGHT (jsdom won't catch this): make the DriverLayout <Content> itself position:relative and absolute-fill the MapLayer against Content directly (inset:0), rather than relying on a height:100% chain, so the map gets a definite size and does not collapse to zero height. Reuse useOwnStatusSync(meData?.driverId) and useRouteToast for the return-Home toast (CLAUDE.md laneB3c driver route toast). Preserve the push-subscription ensureSubscribed() effect + the Permissions API geolocation check from DriverHomePage.

RE-HOME the session ride hooks that lived inside the DELETED DriverRidePage (advisor trap #1 — do NOT lose these): useRideRestore(myDriverId), useLiveClear(myDriverId) (F-04 mid-ride reassignment), useWakeLock(order != null), useActiveOrder() (order + no-show timer), useQueuePendingCount(), and the runTransition wrapper that sets a reconciledNote on outcome.type==='stale' (the reassigned banner). DriverMapScreen owns useRideTransition and passes arrive/start/onComplete(->navigate('/driver/ride/complete'))/onNoShow + isPending + pendingCount + reconciledNote down to RideSheet. The offline queue + reconcile + PendingBadge behavior is preserved end-to-end.

Active-ride map: compute leg = selectRouteLeg({status, hasDropoff}) (WI-1), fetch geometry via useRouteGeometry (WI-3, refetch on status change), compute cameraTarget points via selectDriverMapCamera({own, legStart:own, legEnd: legEndpoint(leg, order)}) (WI-1), and pass own/pickup/dropoff/routeGeometry/cameraTarget to DriverMapInner. ETA to RideSheet from useRouteGeometry.durationSeconds (ceil to minutes) or useOfferRoute. While an OFFER is showing (before accept) the offer's driver->pickup line MAY be drawn (spec section 2 optional) — acceptable to defer; if drawn, thread the offer pickup as the leg endpoint.

DriverLayout.tsx: swap the <OfferTakeover .../> render for <OfferCard dto expiresAt onDismiss={clearOffer}/> (the offer box stays SESSION-WIDE in DriverLayout so an offer arriving on /driver/history still shows Accept/Decline — DESIGN DECISION surfaced, no regression vs today). KEEP useFleetHub(), useOfferListener(), DriverPositionReporter, DriverQueueBar, and the enableSilentRefresh('/driver/login')+scheduleProactiveRefresh boot effect. BOTTOM-EDGE CONTRACT (advisor): the ride RideSheet (shared/ui/BottomSheet, position:fixed bottom:0) and the BottomNav both anchor the bottom edge and would collide during a ride. Resolution = HIDE the BottomNav while an active ride is in progress (mirrors the customer app where the sheet owns the bottom; keeps WI-4's shared BottomSheet UNCHANGED — no offset prop needed). Implement in DriverLayout: read the active order via useActiveOrderStore(s => s.order) with an ATOMIC selector (module-level zustand, readable here) and render the BottomNav only when order == null (i.e. not on an active ride). When there is no active ride the BottomNav renders exactly as today (Home/History/Settings) so Settings/History stay reachable. Remove the OfferTakeover import.

router.tsx: the /driver index child renders <DriverMapScreen/>; DELETE the { path: 'ride', element: <DriverRidePage/> } child and the DriverHomePage + DriverRidePage imports. KEEP { path: 'ride/complete', element: <CompletePage/> }, history, settings, and /driver/login. DriverMapScreen is a CHILD of DriverLayout (unlike the customer sibling pattern) because DriverLayout hosts the session hub/offer/position mounts — do NOT make it a sibling.

REMOVE with no dangling references (tsc is the gate): DriverHomePage.tsx, DriverRidePage.tsx + DriverRidePage.test.tsx, OfferTakeover.tsx, RideMapStrip.tsx + RideMapStrip.test.tsx, and RideMapInner.tsx (superseded by DriverMapInner — grep-confirm nothing else imports it before deleting; keep if still referenced). Grep-confirm no remaining import of any removed module anywhere (router, DriverLayout, tests). Settings/History/Complete/Login screens and all reused hooks keep functioning.
